worlds.name: water
worlds.notes: Polar protic, high dielectric; dissolves ions; attacks delta+ Si. Earth reference.

worlds.name: ammonia
worlds.notes: Liquid 195-240 K at 1 atm. Dielectric ~22 at 239 K (higher when colder). Basic/nucleophilic: ammonolysis expected to attack Si like water; Si chemistry in NH3 'has not been studied'.

worlds.name: titan
worlds.notes: Non-polar aprotic cryosolvent, dielectric ~1.7. Almost no solvolysis, but solubility tiny (SiH4 ppt in N2, glycine-size <ppm) and reactions ~1e-19 x slower (Ea 50).

worlds.name: venus_clouds
worlds.notes: Venus clouds 48-60 km, <100 C, <2 bar. Electrophilic, dehydrating. Most Earth biochemicals degrade fast but nucleobases/most amino acids stable; dipeptides solvolyse within weeks. Larger share of Si chemical space stable than in water. Dielectric value for H2SO4 is ~100 (25 C) per Gillespie & Cole 1956 title-verified only.

worlds.name: magma
worlds.notes: Silicate melt; Si-O bonds broken on ms timescale; no persistent molecular information.

knobs.name: Group 14 backbone (C <-> Si <-> Ge slider)
knobs.controls: interpolates self_bond, bond_to_O, pi_bond_ability, electronegativity of the backbone type
knobs.physical_meaning: Going down group 14 the atom gets bigger and less electronegative: X-X single bond 346 -> 222 -> ~188 kJ/mol, pi bond 274 -> 97 kJ/mol, X-O bond 358 -> 452 kJ/mol
knobs.emergent_effect: [INFERRED] Carbon end: long chains, rings and double-bond motifs persist -> high motif diversity. Silicon end: chains short-lived in polar solvents, few rigid/unsaturated motifs, O captures Si into inert silica blocks -> reef/sand worlds

knobs.name: Bond count (valence / hypervalency)
knobs.controls: maxBonds per particle 1-6; hypervalent toggle lets Si/P/S hold 5-6 transiently
knobs.physical_meaning: Valence 1 terminates, 2 makes chains/rings, 3-4 branches/networks. Si can be 5-6-coordinate; the 5-coordinate intermediate speeds both catalysis and hydrolysis
knobs.emergent_effect: [INFERRED] valence <=2: only chains and rings, no complex branching; 4: tree-like polymers and catalytic sets; 5-6: faster reaction but faster decay (trade-off)

knobs.name: Oxygen hunger
knobs.controls: ratio bond_to_O / self_bond (C 1.03, Si 2.04) -> probability a backbone atom next to O converts irreversibly to an oxide sink
knobs.physical_meaning: Si-O (452) is far stronger than Si-Si (222); SiO2 polymerises into insoluble solid; making SiH4 from silica costs +434 kJ/mol vs methane from CO2 -142
knobs.emergent_effect: [INFERRED] high hunger: oxide waste accumulates as solid, entombs organisms, energy budget drains; low hunger (C): gaseous waste diffuses away, clean recycling

knobs.name: Solvent
knobs.controls: world preset: solvent_attack per element, dielectric, solubility/mobility
knobs.physical_meaning: Protic polar solvents (water, NH3) attack delta+ Si; aprotic cryosolvents attack nothing but dissolve almost nothing; conc. H2SO4 is electrophilic and spares Si relative to water
knobs.emergent_effect: [INFERRED] water: Si worlds stall at 'first chain'; Titan/N2: Si chains survive but nothing meets (no metabolism); H2SO4: Si-C hybrids thrive (best Si world)

knobs.name: Temperature
knobs.controls: global kT -> Arrhenius rate factor for both bond making and breaking; clamped to solvent liquid range
knobs.physical_meaning: k ~ exp(-Ea/RT). Ea=50 kJ/mol: 94 K is ~1e-19 x, 220 K ~7e-4 x, 330 K ~6 x, 1500 K ~1e7 x the 300 K rate. Petkowski cites 2-3 x drop per 10 C
knobs.emergent_effect: [INFERRED] Goldilocks band: too cold = frozen museum (bonds last but no reactions), too hot = soup that never holds structure. Weak bonds (Si-Si) need colder worlds; use log-compressed rate in the sim

knobs.name: Energy source
knobs.controls: rate and type of energy injection: UV (surface/cloud top), redox gradient (vents), thermal cycling, radiolysis
knobs.physical_meaning: Life needs disequilibrium: chemosynthesis and photosynthesis on Earth; radiolytic H2 powers a single-species ecosystem 2.8 km down; Titan C2H2 + 3H2 -> 2CH4 proposed
knobs.emergent_effect: [INFERRED] localised sources (vents) give patchy ecosystems and competition for hotspots; diffuse UV gives surface mats; low energy + slow T = sparse life

steelman.scenario: Sulfuric-acid hybrid: carbon + silicon co-backbone in Venus-like cloud droplets
steelman.conditions: 81-98% H2SO4, ~280-370 K, <2 bar, sunlight; Si as common heteroatom (Si-Si, Si-C, Si-H bonds); needs a peptide-bond substitute
steelman.status: plausible/theorised (strongest Si case in the literature)

steelman.scenario: Cryogenic nitrogen/methane world with mostly-silicon chemistry
steelman.conditions: aprotic liquid N2 (63-77 K, Triton, cold planets far from M dwarfs) or CH4/C2H6 (~94 K, Titan); unsaturated/reactive Si species to beat the cold; silanes more soluble in N2 than carbon species
steelman.status: plausible/theorised, disfavoured (solubility: SiH4 only ppt in N2; 'any biochemistry implausible in cryosolvents')

steelman.scenario: Carbon life that recruits silicon: Si-C enzymes, biosilica armour, clay-template origins
steelman.conditions: water, carbon backbone; Si used structurally (diatoms, sponges) or as specialised heteroatom (evolved cytochrome c makes Si-C bonds); optionally silicate clay scaffolds at the origin
steelman.status: consensus for biosilica & lab Si-C enzymes; plausible/theorised (minority) for clay genes

steelman.scenario: REJECTED: high pressure makes silicon carbon-like
steelman.status: no support found: pressure pushes Si to higher coordination (6-coordinate network solids, e.g. stishovite) and makes CARBON silicon-like (quartz-like CO2-V above 40 GPa/1800 K), the reverse of what the idea needs [INFERRED from cited result]
